wrong.why: This Jediael belongs to Benjamin's genealogy and is identified with Ashbel in Bilhan's supplied record, whereas jediael denotes Shimri's son.
The Hebrew names Aher as Hushim's father and does not identify him as Ehi.
Shallum is explicitly among Naphtali's sons, so the concluding sons-of-Bilhah designation describes ancestry through the named intervening generation.
The Hebrew names Sheresh immediately before 'his sons, Ulam and Rakem,' assigning those sons to Sheresh rather than Peresh.
Ulam and Rakem are named as the sons of the immediately preceding Sheresh rather than Peresh.
Resheph is coordinated with Rephah without a following 'his son,' so the verse does not make Resheph Rephah's son.
Shilshah and Beera both occur in Zophah's list of sons, with no statement that Shilshah descends from Beera.

missing.why: The verse includes Jahziel in Naphtali's named sons and identifies that lineage as sons of Bilhah.
The verse includes Guni in Naphtali's named sons and identifies that lineage as sons of Bilhah.
The verse includes Jezer in Naphtali's named sons and identifies that lineage as sons of Bilhah.
Zabad 'his son' continues the genealogy immediately after the second Tahath in verse 20.
Laadan 'his son' continues the genealogy immediately after Tahan in verse 25.
Non 'his son' continues the genealogy immediately after Elishama in verse 26.
Serah is explicitly called the sister of the listed sons of Asher, including Imnah.
Arah is explicitly listed as Ulla's son, with Ulla identified as Jephunneh in Arah's supplied record.
Rezia is explicitly listed as Ulla's son, with Ulla identified as Jephunneh in Rizia's supplied record.
